comment: script → statements per dialect. `all` = the same in every dialect.

cases.name: line comment
cases.script:
select 1 -- no; split
from t; select 2

cases.name: block comment
cases.script: select 1 /* nor; here */ from t; select 2

cases.name: dollar quoting
cases.script: create function f() returns int as $$ begin return 1; end; $$ language plpgsql; select f()
statements: create function f() returns int as $$ begin return 1; end; $$ language plpgsql

cases.name: dollar inside a name is no quote
DELIMITER
statements: create procedure p() begin select 1; select 2; end

cases.name: delimiter as a column name is no command
GO inside a line is a name
GO in a string or comment is text
trigger keeps its inner statements
cases.script: create trigger t after insert on a begin update b set n = n + 1; insert into log values (1); end; select 1
statements: create trigger t after insert on a begin update b set n = n + 1; insert into log values (1); end

cases.name: trigger with CASE … END inside
cases.script: create temp trigger t after update on a begin update b set n = case when 1 then 2 else 3 end; end; select 1
statements: create temp trigger t after update on a begin update b set n = case when 1 then 2 else 3 end; end

cases.name: BEGIN of a transaction is no block
cases.script: begin; insert into t values (1); end; select 1

cases.name: PL/SQL keeps its semicolons and ends at the slash
a routine, then statements
PL/SQL without a slash runs to the end
cases.script:
declare n number;
begin n := 4 / 2; end;
statements:
declare n number;
begin n := 4 / 2; end;

cases.name: a slash line ends a plain statement too, a division does not
cases.script:
select 4
 / 2 from dual
/
select 2 from dual
/

cases.name: q-quotes hold quotes and semicolons
cases.script: select q'[it's; fine]' from dual; select nq'{a'b;c}' from dual; select 3 from dual

cases.name: create table and view are no PL/SQL
cases.script: create table t (id number); create or replace view v as select 1 x from dual; insert into t values (1);
statements: create or replace view v as select 1 x from dual

cases.name: a comment before a block
statements:
-- setup; really
/* a; b */ begin null; end;

cases.name: dollar quotes keep their semicolons
cases.script: create macro f() as $$a;b$$; select f(); select 'x;y'

cases.name: SET TERM of isql names the end of a statement
cases.script:
SET TERM ^ ;
CREATE PROCEDURE p AS BEGIN delete from t; END^
SET TERM ; ^
select 1 from rdb$database; select 2 from rdb$database
statements: CREATE PROCEDURE p AS BEGIN delete from t; END

cases.name: a long comment, a sub-routine and an external function
cases.script:
/*  */
create procedure p as begin delete from t; end; execute block as declare procedure s as begin delete from t; end declare v int; begin v = 1; end; create function f (a int) returns int external name 'm!f' engine udr as 'x;y'; select 1 from rdb$database
statements:
/*  */
create procedure p as begin delete from t; end
execute block as declare procedure s as begin delete from t; end declare v int; begin v = 1; end
create function f (a int) returns int external name 'm!f' engine udr as 'x;y'

cases.name: comments with #, strings of three quotes, no doubled quote
cases.script:
select a # customer's id; not here
from d.t; select ''' ' ; ''' as s; select 'it\'s; one', `a\`;b` from d.t; select 'a' 'b;c'
statements:
select a # customer's id; not here
from d.t

cases.name: comments with //, strings between $$ and backslash escapes
cases.script:
select 1 // it's; not here
; create procedure p() returns int language sql as $$ begin delete from t; return 1; end; $$; select 'it\'s; one'
statements: create procedure p() returns int language sql as $$ begin delete from t; return 1; end; $$

cases.name: a block of Snowflake Scripting keeps its semicolons
cases.script: declare n int default 0; begin drop table if exists t; for i in 1 to 3 do n := n + i; end for; if (n > 3) then begin transaction; delete from t; commit; else n := case when n = 0 then 1 else n end; end if; return n; end; select 1; begin; select 2
statements: declare n int default 0; begin drop table if exists t; for i in 1 to 3 do n := n + i; end for; if (n > 3) then begin transaction; delete from t; commit; else n := case when n = 0 then 1 else n end; end if; return n; end

cases.name: a procedure of Snowflake without $$ is one statement, a quoted name ends at its quote
cases.script: create procedure p() returns int language sql as begin let c cursor for select a from t; while (true) loop break; end loop; return 1; end; select "a\\"; select 3
statements: create procedure p() returns int language sql as begin let c cursor for select a from t; while (true) loop break; end loop; return 1; end

cases.name: a compound statement of SQL PL keeps its semicolons
cases.script: create procedure p(in n int) language sql begin declare i int default 0; again: loop set i = i + 1; if i > n then leave again; end if; end loop again; delete from t where a = case when i > 3 then 1 else 2 end; end; select 1 from sysibm.sysdummy1; begin atomic insert into t values (1); end; values 2
statements: create procedure p(in n int) language sql begin declare i int default 0; again: loop set i = i + 1; if i > n then leave again; end if; end loop again; delete from t where a = case when i > 3 then 1 else 2 end; end
begin atomic insert into t values (1); end

cases.name: a body in PSQL keeps its semicolons
cases.script: execute block as declare n integer; begin n = 1; if (n = 1) then begin delete from t; end end; create or alter trigger tr for t before insert as begin new.id = case when new.id is null then 1 else new.id end; end; alter trigger tr inactive; select 1 from rdb$database; begin_work
statements: execute block as declare n integer; begin n = 1; if (n = 1) then begin delete from t; end end
create or alter trigger tr for t before insert as begin new.id = case when new.id is null then 1 else new.id end; end

cases.name: a backslash is a character, a quote is doubled
